description: A gotogether binding file (gotogether.binding/2): how a Go program's recorded steps become calls of a Quint model's actions. Generated from the Go type that reads it (GOTOGETHER_UPDATE_SCHEMA=1 go test ./schemas/).

args.description: Args maps model parameters to Quint expression templates over the step (see StepData). A parameter not given is the step field of the same name, converted by the parameter's type (Param.DefaultTemplate): `{{.p}}`, or `{{ toSet .p }}` for a set, toList for a list, toMap for a map. An action whose parameters all default needs no entry.

expect.description: Expect is a Quint boolean over the post-state that must hold after the step: the observed state projection (quint.obs.*) checked against the model's state.

outcomes.description: Outcomes overrides the binding's outcome map for this action. "skip" drops steps with that outcome (the model has no such step); "call" replays them like successful ones. A non-ok outcome of an action whose templates ignore .outcome must be mapped here, or generation fails.

actions.description: Actions maps a model action to the templates that build its call.

actors.description: Actors are the actors whose traces the binding checks: glob patterns (* any run of characters, / and . included, since an actor's name is no path: `*.clients` matches `t/x.clients`; ? one character; [a-z] and [!a-z] a class; \c the character c), a pattern written "!p" excluding the actors p matches. Empty: every actor. A trace of another actor is another binding's, left out of every check and of StepsToITF, and named with its step count in the report's issues: so one run that records two sides (a system's commits under the tenants' names, its clients' calls under "<tenant>.clients") is checked by two bindings of one model, `actors: ["!*.clients"]` and `actors: ["*.clients"]`. Every step still reconstructs, so a gap or a settle is found over the whole run (Reconstruct).

antecedents.description: Antecedents name, per invariant, the condition under which it says something (Quint over the model's state): where it never holds, the invariant holds vacuously. An invariant `A implies B` has A without saying so (Model.Antecedents); give one for any other form, such as `xs.forall(x => P(x) implies Q(x))`, whose antecedent is `xs.exists(x => P(x))`.

complete.description: Complete says every run checked against the binding is a finished one (a whole journey, settled, every call answered), not a prefix: `gotogether validate` then fails one that is not, as with -require-finish. It needs an eventual val, the journey's end: without one a settled prefix would pass. Tests state it as a claim instead (qtest.Finishes), which this does not change.

constants.description: Constants of the instance, as Quint expressions. They are templates over the whole trace (see Stats), so bounds can follow what was seen.

defs.description: Defs is Quint text added to the generated module (helpers for templates).

diagnosticEvidence.description: DiagnosticEvidence relates model diagnostic items to observed model calls.

eventually.description: Eventually are vals of the model that must hold when the run ends (no work pending: `outbox.size() == 0`): liveness obligations, checked in the last observed state only, and only of a trace that recorded its system settled (a settle record: qenv's Sim.Settle, or qobs.Settled), where pending work is a failure to finish rather than a run cut short. Every check honours it: explorations, Record, Validate, qhegel and the CLI.

format.description: Format, if set, names the binding format the file is written in (FormatName): a binding of another major is refused with the fix (upgrade gotogether for a later one, rewrite an earlier one), not with its keys "unknown". Empty: the current one.

hidden.description: Hidden are model actions that happen and are never recorded (a gossip round, a handoff): between recorded steps any sequence of them, at most HiddenDepth long (default 4), may have run. Each takes no parameters (give the model a wrapper that picks them with nondet). A trace is then judged by the Go evaluator, which searches the states they reach: quint cannot replay a step whose choices are unknown.

intern.description: Intern maps an argument name to a scope ("actor" or "process"). Its observed values (opaque ids like "g20260924T101500") are renamed 1, 2, 3, ... in order of first appearance: the abstraction function from implementation identifiers to the model's small integers.

invariants.description: Invariants are vals of the model checked in every observed state.

outcomes.description: Outcomes maps a recorded quint.outcome to a Quint expression, available to templates as .outcome. Actions may override it.

partition.description: Partition is the argument naming each step's entity (a charge's id, an account), for a serial log of entities the model treats independently: each entity's steps are judged alone, in parallel, in the whole log's instance, every failing entity reported (a log judged whole stops at its first failure). Sound only if the model factors by it: a step of one entity reads and writes only entries, keyed by its own, of the state's maps, and each invariant is a conjunction of foralls over a map's keys judging an entry at a time. validate checks it on each run's own evaluation and refuses a run where it does not hold, naming the step and the entry (DESIGN §66).

restart.description: Restart is the model action inserted where an actor's process changes: the crash a dead process cannot report. Empty: a process change is an error.

resume.description: Resume is a nullary model action whose nondet picks give the states a trace that lost its prefix may start in (bounded by the model's constants and invariants: action resumeAny = nondet b = 0.to(LIMIT) .oneOf() all { balance' = b, ops' = 0 }). A trace whose first recorder lost its prefix, with no snapshot step at its head, is judged from those states by the Go evaluator's search (quint confirms its verdict): it conforms if some admitted state explains the rest. A snapshot step, where there is one, is used instead.

simulate.description: Simulate says what the model alone does with its invariants (`gotogether simulate`): which it guarantees, which it allows to fail.

allows.description: Allows are the invariants the model allows to fail: some trace must violate each, or checking the code against it proves nothing. An eventual val here is the code's to drive: the model may stay with it false forever (its actions are observations, a probe's), so `simulate -graph` reports such a cycle without failing.

constants.description: Constants override the binding's for the simulation: those that are templates over a run (`{{ set "node" }}`) need a value here.

holds.description: Holds are the invariants the model guarantees: no trace violates them. An eventual val here is one the model drives itself: `simulate -graph` fails on a fair cycle that keeps it false forever (P6).

possible.description: Possible are what the model must be able to do (Possible): some trace reaches each. A model too strict to reach a scenario a conforming run would show fails `gotogether simulate` here, before any code is checked against it.

anyOf.description: a Quint predicate over the state, an action's name, or a call naming some of its parameters' values: reserve(result = "refused")

steps.description: model actions some trace takes in this order, each a name or a call

when.description: a Quint predicate over the model's state

search.description: Search bounds the Go evaluator's every search of the model on its own: `simulate -graph`'s state graph, the possibles' search, and qtest.Model's claims.

depth.description: Depth bounds a search's paths from init (default none): one only it cut saw every state within Depth steps.

states.description: States bounds the states a search visits (default 100000): one it cut proves nothing past them.

skip.description: Skip, if set, says why the model is not run on its own: a replay-only model, whose actions take observed values, has no step to simulate.

steps.description: Steps and Samples bound the run (default 30 and 1000).

terminal.description: Terminal is a Quint predicate over the state saying where the model means to stop: `gotogether simulate -graph` reports a state the step cannot leave as a deadlock unless it holds there (a protocol that has finished, a log at its bound). A state the step can leave only by a stutter (a read) is never a deadlock, so a model that can always read needs none: the report counts such states as quiet.

unfair.description: Unfair and Stops are the step's actions `simulate -graph`'s liveness search does not hold to weak fairness (every other action is weakly fair: one enabled throughout a cycle must be taken in it, a stutter counting for nothing). An unfair action obliges nothing and may run forever (a client's input, which may come or not); an action that stops is never taken in a cycle (a fault, which a settle turns off, or an input the driver stops sending before it settles).

verifySkip.description: VerifySkip, if set, says why -verify skips the model: one Apalache cannot encode, or one too slow at any useful depth. Its sampling stands.

verifySteps.description: VerifySteps caps `gotogether simulate -verify` for this model: Apalache's cost grows steeply with depth, and differently by model (0: no cap).

snapshot.description: Snapshot is a model action whose parameters are the whole state (it assigns every variable from them: restore(balance, ops)): a step of it first in its trace is the state the trace starts from, instead of init. A log that lost its prefix (rotated, truncated, a recorder started mid-run) is judged from the snapshot recorded at its head; a snapshot step anywhere else is skipped, with an issue.

spec.description: Spec is the .qnt file (relative to the binding file) and Module the parameterised module in it to instantiate.

within.description: Within are bounded-response obligations: each time a val (After) becomes true, another (Holds) must hold within Bound of virtual (or recorded) time, in the replay's states, timed by their steps. A trace that ends before the bound with the obligation open is no verdict, unless it recorded its system settled (nothing changes after). Every check of a run honours it.

bound.description: BoundText is the bound as written
